Pick the best offer — the contract is generated automatically and both sides sign it with an electronic signature.

insights.title: Understand What Moves the Market.
insights.subtitle: Short, practical reads for wholesale buyers and sellers.

articles.dek: How supply, demand, costs and expectations shape a price.
body: Wholesale prices mostly follow the balance of supply and demand: a big harvest or more imports pushes prices down, shrinking stocks push them up. Fuel, transport and storage costs feed directly into the price too.
Expectations matter as well: when sellers expect prices to rise, they hold stock back. That is why the trend over several weeks is a more reliable signal than any single day's price.
Fruit and vegetable prices are usually lowest at harvest and then climb as storage costs grow and stocks shrink. Greenhouse produce costs more in winter because heating and lighting are added.
When planning long-term purchases, a full year of price history is useful — it shows where the seasonal highs and lows fall.

articles.dek: Farmers' bazaars, wholesale centres and warehouses.
body: Farmers' bazaars lean toward retail and small wholesale, while wholesale centres handle large volumes and steady supply. Warehouses usually deal in construction materials and goods that store well.
In wholesale, minimum order quantities, packaging and delivery terms matter as much as price — always compare them together.
A fair comparison starts with total cost: quantity × unit price + delivery. A low unit price can be wiped out by expensive delivery.
Then check the grade, whether the supplier is verified and how it is rated, available stock and minimum order. Bozor-Analitika weighs exactly these factors in its recommendation score.

articles.dek: Why the same product costs differently across regions.
body: Prices tend to be lower where a product is grown and higher in large consumption centres, where transport and demand add to the cost.
If the gap is larger than the delivery cost, buying from another region can pay off — a regional comparison plus a total-cost calculation shows it quickly.

items.a: A B2B platform that brings buyers, wholesalers, farmers and market administrators together: wholesale prices, offer comparison, market analytics and an AI analyst.
Shops, supermarkets, restaurants and manufacturers (buyers), and farmers, wholesale traders and distributors (sellers).

items.q: Where does the market data come from?
items.a: Sellers publish prices and offers on the platform. Every price shows its source, the supplier's verification status and when it was last updated.

items.q: Does the platform provide real-time information?
items.a: An offer updates as soon as the seller changes it, and every change is written to the price history. Each price shows when it was updated, so you can always see how fresh it is.

items.q: How does the AI analyst work?
items.a: The language model has no direct database access: it can only call the platform's analytics tools and writes its answer from their results. It never invents prices, suppliers or statistics.

footer.privacyBody: We store only the data needed to run the service: account details, published offers and requests. Passwords are stored encrypted. Data is never sold to third parties. Contact an administrator to delete your account.
footer.termsBody: Sellers are responsible for the accuracy of the prices and details they publish. The platform connects buyers and sellers but is not a party to the deal. Suspicious or inaccurate offers are moderated and may be removed.

about.title: Making Uzbekistan's markets transparent
about.lead: Bozor-Analitika is a B2B platform that brings buyers, wholesalers, farmers and market administrators into one digital ecosystem. It was built for the Chamber of Commerce's Case #19.
about.problemD: Market information is fragmented across bazaars, phone calls and Telegram groups. Entrepreneurs lose time and money.
about.solutionD: A structured offer database, total-cost comparison, price history, supply and demand indicators, and an AI analyst grounded in data.
principles: Every price shows its source, verification status and last-updated time.
Suspicious prices are excluded from statistics and sent to moderation.
The AI never invents prices, suppliers or statistics.
